# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Gender:** male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** a crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a peculiar, anxious, restless small man.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039)_

## Personality

Mr. Pettifer is considered eccentric and short-tempered, though he can also be gentle, amiable, and anxious once his temper passes. He is outspokenly averse to traditional domestic routines and maintains his house without women. He is considered stingy by locals, though he displays curiosity and neighborliness, and holds a strong affection for his pet parrot.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046)_

## Traits

- eccentric  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- short-tempered  <sub>[v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P9](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0009)</sub>
- stingy  <sub>[v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008)</sub>
- anxious  <sub>[v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039)</sub>
- amiable  <sub>[v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003)</sub>

## History

After purchasing Robert Bell's farm in Brierley, Mr. Pettifer quickly developed a reputation for eccentricity, living alone without women and maintaining irregular dining and dishwashing habits. He hired John Henry Carter of Pale Sands as a farmhand and later employed another clumsy worker. When Nell Harcourt mistakenly sold his Jersey cow after finding it in her field, she visited his home to confess. Though initially quick-tempered, he treated Nell gently and hosted her for tea, leading the two to form a friendly relationship. Nell later confided in him about her ambition to write a story, though he gave her little encouragement, remarking that too much rubbish was already published.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P16](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0016), [v2 c3 P35](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0035), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v3 c11 P42](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0042), [v3 c11 P50](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0050)_

## Background by volume

- Purchased Robert Bell's farm on St. Brendan's Island next to the Abernethy place  <sub>[v2 c1 P0](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0000), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Hails from New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Received his pet parrot Nutmeg from his brother, a seafaring man  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006), [v2 c3 P38](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0038)</sub>

## Quotes

> Ignore that parrot. He . . . he utters foolishness constantly. My brother, a seafaring man, gave him to me. A sailor's speech isn't always particularly refined, and birds like parrots copy things easily.  <sub>[v2 c3 P6](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0006)</sub>

> It seems you possess a bit of a temper. I suppose that accompanies hair of your shade. Brierley is quite a nice location or I would not have settled here; however, I assume even you will agree it possesses a few shortcomings?  <sub>[v2 c3 P42](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0042)</sub>

> To be wedded to the flawless wife would prove even more unpleasant  <sub>[v2 c3 P44](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0044)</sub>

> You could come over and speak with me now and then. The distance isn't great and people should show neighborliness. I feel a bit intrigued by that society of yours. It appears to me that it will offer some amusement. Which person will you approach first?  <sub>[v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046)</sub>
